name: Master of International Tourism and Hospitality Management
description: Prepares you to manage hotels, events and visitor experiences in a large city market. Units cover revenue management, service design and destination marketing, taught through case studies of real venues. An industry placement in your second year puts the theory to work.

name: Master of International Tourism and Hospitality Management
description: Tourism along a coast and in wine regions is the setting for this course, which looks at how visitors, local businesses and the environment fit together. You study sustainable tourism, hospitality finance and people management, and finish with a placement or a consulting project for a regional operator.

name: Diploma of Hospitality Management
description: Hands-on training for supervisors and duty managers in restaurants, bars and hotels. You run shifts in the training restaurant, build rosters and budgets, and learn to handle guests and staff. Work placement in a venue is part of the year.
